Columnizer #1
A Note from the Column Government

Dear Schitz,

We as a team are actively improving our local communities by supplying affordable housing to consumers. Our ministries are taking active precautions to make sure that we are addressing the issues seen in Relayer as optimally as possible. Our goal is to benefit all people from all walks of life, race, and gender to ensure a welcome environment for families and businesses alike. The statistics that we use to carefully calculate what and where we build are only from the most trusted Scholar researchers, data analysts, and economists, so we can be proud to say that our developments are eco-friendly.

Thanks, Jannet Smith
Columnizer #2
A Complaint from a Ponderosa Citizen

I'm tired of these tramps coming onto these paths and blocking them when I go for my morning walks. One of them even tried to assault my son, who is only 7, and no one does anything around here! We need more funding for guards around here to wipe out all of the vermin. The government is too damn liberal about these things! Like how they don't increase my pay and increase the reductions instead because of these damn homeless people.
Columnizer #3
A Warning from Pugna of the Volare Guild

This thing is never shut off. Ever. I've seen this thing run for 2 weeks straight without maintenance. It's almost like they don't care about the health of the machines around here. But who cares? The Scholars say it's what humanity needs, so be it.
Columnizer #4
A Note from Pugna of the Volare Guild (it's covered in oil)
It's a shame what happened to this place. No people, just [unreadable]
Columnizer #5
A Page From a Book by Reywas Nesnah

Picture this, if you will. This place used to be a warm, flourishing place with birds and other animals that would be commonly seen wandering around here everyday. But now, after endless toxic rain, the infrastructure was destroyed, and all businesses lost their jobs. The Faucet Reef spilled out so much oil after the implosion, when the Oil River started to flow, that the people here went in droves to seek the medicinal plants below. Now, as a 15 year old, despite my age I see that this was not a freak accident like most people say. People here are so gullible that they will take everything at face value.
Columnizer #6
An Observation from Scholar Peitharchia Andras

You're gonna pay for this shit. It's impossible to publish anything. You will strike down any potential for publishing. You dictate every word I write. I know why: it's because you don't want me to go “off the rails”, and make us look bad, and maybe say that we did something wrong. 2 years of my life just for it to fly under the radar, just because of you? That last little bit? I've spent so long testing, experimenting, and getting to be in a lab like this one, let alone even becoming a Scholar in the first place. Stop making excuses. Stop being a narcissist. Have some fucking mercy. I'm going to find something new, and I'm taking my research with me.\n- Peitharchia
Columnizer #7
A Note from Pugna of the Volare Guild

Rest. Rest at the base. The great curved pillars of time and life, that stand forever absolute. I realize that this is the gateway to the abyss, but I never thought it could be so beautiful. The step below hell awaits on the true ground.\n\nThe Scholars come here in droves once a year, every year, to look at the progress of the lift. Every year it's just the same. A test subject goes down the lift, either dies, disappears, or comes back up never the same when they descended.

Earth
And

A note:
It seems like everyone here, on this column, is bound to go to the Scholars, and then attempt to try to revolutionize the world but then fall to some nihilism when they sell out. And if you don't become a scholar and were born below Ponderosa, you have no way to climb the ladder. The only true way to be contempt with life, I feel, is to fall back into nature; to go back to the roots. That does not mean to live in faith of God, or Azaprota, as it will push you to anger and destruction, like so many others who will fight and die over land and god.

When the pendulums of your life align from the polyrhythm within, for a moment, in that time and in that moment, you will be inside and outside this experience.

Penistown
11 hours in the tin pan
Where were you?
On a walk.
Anyways, I wonder what it would be like going into another section.\nThe locals would probably kill you,\nbut that's just the way it works, this big tower.
Oh yeah. Yep. It- it's probably the Scholars that do that,\nbut that's a group of people that should be thrown off this column.
I wanted to ask you this. Have you\never encountered the gang, Iudeus?
No. But one of their members I think\nwent to Pre-Scholars here.
Ok. From what I've read I think they're\nanti-symforist, or anti-scholar.
Why are they so prevalent?
They must be very good fighters. They probably train\nVolare all day long when they're not causing chaos.
Well you maybe could beat them up.
Possibly. At least I'm not a moron like they are.
Well...
I think they're against the Scholars too. That's probably\ntheir whole thing. They probably rave about M.J.K.
I just said that.
Every person in Ponderosa is a moron, brainwashed by\nthe Scholars and symforism. Living on false hopes and beliefs.
That gang isn't brainwashed, but they're just like apes,\nconstantly angry and aggressive to anything living.
Even the adults around here are all cultist idiots too,\nprobably reading all 560 pages of The Tale to Symfora every night.
Probably.
Hey. How's it going?
Good.
Great. I've got some news. In the old literary catalog,\nonly 10 texts are left missing. The volunteers have been\nvery effective at finding them.
We've found some random notes and pieces from people\nlaying around the place, so we're organizing them into\na collection named Columnizer.
Ah. This is off topic, but do you happen to\nhave any recommendations for new books?
Well I think that the ones by Maynard J. Kaiser\nwould be interesting to you. Maynard was a very\noutspoken criticizer of symforism, like you.
Well... that's not the full picture.\nYou still want to uphold our anonymity with our\nconversations, correct?
Yes...?
Ok. I hold a few grudges in my life.\nAgainst humans. It has become too much of\na burden to remain here.
Oh. Well, to be blunt, that is a very\negocentric decision. Naive. But,\ndon't take it from me. It's your choice.
I can't keep doing this. The art world,\nthis district, the Scholars, and my school are\nall full of snobs, bigots, cultists and morons.
I can't go anywhere else on this level.\nI know that if I descend I will most likely die,\nbut I see the risk to be inferior to the potential reward.
I don't know how to feel about this.\nHow will you get back?
I'll see.
I guess this might be my last time seeing you.
Perhaps.
Feel free to look at the browser some\nmore before you go.
Thank you.
Goodbye.
You're staying?
No, but I found this note on the way out.\nI think it might be good for Columizer.
Oh, thanks. I'll add it to the collection\nand look at it later. Are you really still leaving?
Yes. Right now.
Well, remember what I told you. I don't know if I'll\nhave the courage to keep my mouth shut.\nThis is beyond me at this point.
You won't hear from me again, and if you do,\nyou won't want to see me.
Goodbye.
Goodbye.
Don't be a fool, get a pool.
Hey, hey, yeah, tell 'em to bring out the lobster!
I wish that this place could just be reset. I wish that the\nScholars didn't exist, I wish that the government wasn't corrupt,
I wish that my peers would stop wasting time, and I wish that\nwhatever god may be, would give a reason for our existence.
Four grudges I guess. This has got to stop. No one cares anymore.\nI've trapped myself. I need to run far away from this rusty cage.
I've got the skills to do it. This is it.\nWhenever I get the chance, I will run. Maybe even tomorrow.
After all, it's the week break tomorrow, which means I\nhave to go to my uncle Sapiens' library; a perfect opportunity.
You see this?! Look at us!
Open the gates! Let us down there!
We're gonna kill all your Scholars if you don't!
Shut the hell up Myran.
Looks like they got locked out\nof their dojo down in the jungle.
Look who it is! Akid!
Get your ass over here.\nThe whole government is watching us now.
You know, I'm trying to get down there too.
Not a chance. Come here.
Well it's almost 10. Could have just waited.\nYou have the keys to the section doors, right?
We just want the government to know.
Why don't you just follow me down there?
Alright, let's go then!
Get his ass, Gorjan!
Look who showed up! I've been waiting for you,\nbut now's the time for you to go home.
How did you get ahead of me ahead of me?
You don't need to know that.
Build more! This place needs more bright minds!
Think about it. I- mean, we needs to go-go-go up.\nAbove. God will take us th-th-there\nwith our Scholars minds.
You need to stop thinking about those things, man.
Dig down! We need to see it! The Scholar tomes say so!
Why? He didn't even lose the key in that hallway.
You shut your goddamn mouth. He betrayed us.
It's Akid!
Nice work, dipshit. You see this guy? This is\nwhat we will do to you! Get on your\nknees! You ass will bow down to me!
One day, I will get my wings. Everyday I wander around\nhere with nothing to do. You hear me asshole?
Everyday is just the same shit over and over again.\nThat's how people go insane.\nAnd you know what they get?
They die in my hands! If God wanted to change this,\nit would change something! But no,\nso we must destroy all livi-
You're twisted.
Don't you ever fucking cut me off again! You made it\nall the way down here just to die!\nYou're the moron! And now look at Lucant here.
Look at what happened to Myran just above. Just like you.\nNo smarter than the rest! No one is smart!\nWhat the hell does being smart even mean!?
Does anything mean something? Nothing matters!\nEveryone should just go to hell,\nand my ass has to be the one to do it!
I understand.
What? That you're going to die?
No you imbecile! My point is what he understands.\nYou know what Gorjan, I've had enough,\njust kill him already.
Fuck!
I see it now...
Scholars? Rebels? morons? No, protesters.\nDo they want to see God?
Let us in! Let us see God! Show the evidence!\nYou lied! The Scholars lied!
Hey, Akid!
Came down here to see God, too?
No. I don't know what I came down here for.
Nothing. That's what. You came down here for no true,\nreal reason. You never have done anything for a real reason.\nIt's all emotions.
I will cut you open and spill them out onto the ground\nin front of these people, right here-
right now!
Where do you think you are? What do you think\nyou've done for yourself?
Are you addicted to pain? Show me,\nwhat moral have your learned, if none at all?
You're ability to leave problems? To think you're\nsome fucking martyr?
I'd think not.
They're here.
Mom is gonna get worried soon,
and super will be on the table.
A note from mom: Remember to head to the\nlibrary to meet with Sapiens.
Parents already left for work. I could leave right now,\nbut I need to confront one of my grudges first.\nIudeus, the gang.
They hang out in the Court around this time. Plus,\nthe gate to the Shallows doesn't open for Ponderosa citizens until 10.\nMight as well explore.
I gotta get out of here.\nI've never seen the security system acitvated before.
It's probably past 10 now,\nI can get down through that gate finally.
I can't be down here. I'm not in the same\nclass as the locals. They'll kill me.
Goddamn Scholars. I forgot about this monstrosity.
Another one! Where did the rest go?
No wonder why they don't teach\nus about this in Pre-Scholars.
That's what nihilism and anger does,\nI guess. So close now...
This must be over soon...
Is it over yet? Did I make it?\nIs this what I get for all this pain?
I don't know what I've changed about myself.\nMaybe nothing. But I know that the way\nto fulfillment must be here, somewhere.
Where else would it be if not at the end of the world?\nI guess I need to confront God first, if it even exists.\nI don't know why I trusted the Scholars on that one.
